questions.q: In 2 Thessalonians 3:6, Paul gives a strict command in the name of the Lord Jesus Christ regarding church members who refuse to work. What does he command the believers to do?
options: To physically force the idle person to work
To give the idle person money from the church offerings
To keep away from any brother who is walking in idleness and not in accord with the tradition received
To promote the idle person to a leadership position
questions.explain: Paul emphasizes the dignity of labor by instructing the church not to enable laziness: "Now we command you, brothers, in the name of our Lord Jesus Christ, that you keep away from any brother who is walking in idleness..."

questions.q: According to Christian teachings, why should people do their lawful work with honor and diligence?
options: So they can boast about their wealth to others
Because honest labor is a way to serve God, provide for one's family, and help those in need
To eventually become powerful enough to oppress their neighbors
Because it is the only way to earn salvation
questions.explain: Christianity teaches that work is a dignified and divine mandate. Working with honor allows believers to reflect Christ, meet personal responsibilities, and possess resources to share with others (Ephesians 4:28, Colossians 3:23).

questions.q: Upon Paul's arrival in Jerusalem (Acts 21:23-24), the church elders advised him to partake in a purification ritual alongside four other men. Why did they ask him to do this?
options: To prove that the rumors were false and that he still respected and lived in observance of the law
Because Paul had contracted leprosy on his missionary journey
To prepare him for a political debate with the Roman governor
Because it was required before anyone could enter the city gates
questions.explain: Rumors claimed Paul was teaching Jews to abandon Moses. The elders said: "Thus all will know that there is nothing in what they have been told about you, but that you yourself also live in observance of the law."

questions.q: While Paul was held in the barracks in Jerusalem, more than forty Jews plotted an ambush to kill him. Who discovered this plot and reported it to the Roman tribune? (Acts 23:16)
options: A sympathetic Pharisee named Gamaliel
One of the Roman centurions on duty
The son of Paul's sister (his nephew)
Silas, who had traveled there to visit him
questions.explain: Acts 23:16 states: "Now the son of Paul's sister heard of their ambush, so he went and entered the barracks and told Paul." Paul then sent him to the tribune.

questions.q: When Paul presented the gospel to the Roman Governor Felix and his wife Drusilla, he reasoned about righteousness, self-control, and the coming judgment. What was Felix's immediate reaction? (Acts 24:25)
options: He laughed and mocked Paul's beliefs.
He immediately repented and was baptized.
He became alarmed and sent Paul away, saying he would call for him when he had an opportunity.
He ordered Paul to be executed on the spot.
questions.explain: The conviction of the Holy Spirit made Felix uncomfortable. "And as he reasoned about righteousness and self-control and the coming judgment, Felix was alarmed and said, 'Go away for the present. When I get an opportunity I will summon you.'"

questions.q: In 1 Corinthians 13:1, Paul describes the necessity of love in the Christian walk. He writes that if he speaks in the tongues of men and of angels, but has not love, he is merely what?
options: A false prophet
A noisy gong or a clanging cymbal
A blind guide leading the blind
A wandering star in the night
questions.explain: Paul emphasizes that spiritual gifts without love are hollow: "If I speak in the tongues of men and of angels, but have not love, I am a noisy gong or a clanging cymbal."

questions.q: After Paul presented his profound personal testimony and defense before King Agrippa (Acts 26), what memorable response did the king give?
options: "In a short time would you persuade me to be a Christian?"
"You have convinced me, I will follow your God."
"You are mad, your great learning is driving you mad!"
"I sentence you to life in a Roman prison."
questions.explain: While Festus was the one who shouted that Paul's learning was driving him mad, King Agrippa said to Paul, "In a short time would you persuade me to be a Christian?" (Acts 26:28).

questions.q: To demonstrate the dignity of labor, Paul reminded the Thessalonian church of his own personal work ethic while living among them. What did he say he did? (2 Thessalonians 3:8)
options: He lived in luxury, supported entirely by wealthy believers.
He demanded daily wages from the church treasury.
He worked with his hands in toil and labor night and day so as not to be a burden.
He refused to work and focused solely on preaching.
questions.explain: Paul led by example, writing: "...nor did we eat anyone's bread without paying for it, but with toil and labor we worked night and day, that we might not be a burden to any of you."

questions.q: During Paul's imprisonment in Caesarea under Governor Felix (Acts 24:26), Felix sent for Paul frequently and conversed with him. What was Felix secretly hoping to get from Paul?
options: A detailed explanation of Jewish prophecy
A bribe (money) so that he would release him
Information about a rebellion against Rome
A miraculous healing for his sick daughter
questions.explain: Acts 24:26 exposes the governor's corruption: "At the same time he hoped that money would be given him by Paul. So he sent for him often and conversed with him."

questions.q: The Apostle Paul taught the dignity of labor and also practiced it himself so he would not be a burden to the churches. What was Paul's trade or occupation? (Acts 18:3)
options: A fisherman
A tax collector
A tentmaker
A carpenter
questions.explain: When Paul visited Corinth, he stayed with Aquila and Priscilla, "and because he was of the same trade he stayed with them and worked, for they were tentmakers by trade." (Acts 18:3)

questions.q: In teaching believers about obedience to constituted authorities in Romans 13:7, Paul said to pay everyone what is owed them. He mentions taxes, revenue, and which two other things?
options: Tithes and offerings
Sacrifices and burnt offerings
Respect and honor
Food and clothing
questions.explain: Paul wrote: "Pay to all what is owed to them: taxes to whom taxes are owed, revenue to whom revenue is owed, respect to whom respect is owed, honor to whom honor is owed."

questions.q: During Paul's arrest in Jerusalem, the Roman tribune ordered that he be examined by flogging. What crucial piece of information did Paul reveal that made the soldiers stop immediately? (Acts 22:25-29)
options: He revealed that he was a personal friend of King Herod.
He stated that he was a Roman citizen by birth.
He offered the tribune a large bribe of gold.
He prophesied an impending earthquake.
questions.explain: Paul asked the centurion, "Is it lawful for you to flog a man who is a Roman citizen and uncondemned?" When the tribune heard that Paul was a citizen by birth, those who were about to examine him withdrew.

questions.q: In his renowned chapter on Love (1 Corinthians 13:13), Paul concludes by identifying the three things that will endure forever. They are faith, hope, and love. Which of these does he declare to be the greatest?
options: Faith
Hope
Love
They are perfectly equal.
questions.explain: Paul concludes the chapter profoundly: "So now faith, hope, and love abide, these three; but the greatest of these is love."

questions.q: When addressing the Jewish council in Acts 23:3, Paul reacted strongly when the high priest Ananias ordered him to be struck on the mouth. What sharp phrase did Paul use to rebuke him?
options: "You brood of vipers!"
"God is going to strike you, you whitewashed wall!"
"Woe to you, hypocrite!"
"You son of the devil!"
questions.explain: In a moment of intense provocation, Paul cried out, "God is going to strike you, you whitewashed wall! Are you sitting to judge me according to the law, and yet contrary to the law you order me to be struck?"

questions.q: In his final defense before Governor Festus and King Agrippa, Paul summarized his entire ministry and the essence of the gospel by declaring that "the Christ must suffer and that, by being the first to rise from the dead, he would proclaim ________ both to our people and to the Gentiles." (Acts 26:23)
options: wealth
light
law
war
questions.explain: Paul succinctly captures the message of salvation for both Jews and Gentiles by saying: "...he would proclaim light both to our people and to the Gentiles."
